lawyer:
AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate with Md Ershad Hossain Dashed, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Abdus Salam Mandol, with Khandakar Nazrul Islam, Advocates—For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Habib Khan (Md) and others -------- Petitioners
vs
Md Sultan Ali and others -------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-1-2014 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Appeal No. 54 of 2011 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 28-11-2010 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Muktagacha, Mymensingh in Other Class Suit No. 49 of 2009 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the opposite parties, as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 49 of 2009 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Muktagacha, Mymensingh against the petitioners and one Ramjan Ali Khan, as defendant, for a decree of permanent injunction, stating that the property under SA Khatian No. 200 and RS Khatian No. 412 measuring 1.20 sataks belong to Md Hatem Ali and Ahmed Ali. BRS Khatian stand recorded in their names as per their share. Hatem Ali is owner of 80 sataks and Ahmed Ali is owner of 40 sataks. While they were in possession of the property amicably by partition, Hatem Ali by a sale deed No. 3249 dated 1-4-1997 transferred 10 sataks land and by another Deed No. 9623 dated 7-1-1998 transferred 22 sataks, totaling 32 sataks to the plaintiffs and delivered possession to them on the northern side of the plot. 

3. The plaintiff after purchase filled up the low land constructed house thereon, started business in the premises by plaintiff Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 5 and let out some portion to Shadat Hossain, Ayen Ali, Akkas Ali and Liakat Ali on monthly rents and planted various type of trees in the vacant land. While the plaintiff went to mutate their names in the khatian, they found that in the two purchase deeds the plot number and khatian number wrongly written. Thereafter, they propose their vendor for correction of the deed, accordingly, Hatem Ali by two registered declaration No. 3744 and 3745 both dated 13-9-2006 rectified the error by substituting BRS Khatian No. 412 and plot 2565 in place of BRS Khatian No. 172 and Plot No. 2562. Thereafter, said Ahmed Ali from his 40 sataks share transferred 13 sataks, of land to one Shafiar by registered deed No 6244 dated 09-8-2000 and 16.25 sataks to defendant No. 4 Abu Bakker Siddique by deed No. 6243 and by a deed No. 6245 transferred 7.25 sataks to Shahera totalling 36.75 sataks. After transfer there remains only 3.25 sataks land and said Ahmed Ali by a registered deed No. 9025 dated 18-12-2005 transferred 4 sataks of land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in excess of his share but delivered possession in 3.25 sataks in place of 4 sataks. 

4. Defendant No. 1 while in possession on the northern-east side of their purchased land measuring 3.25 sataks there has been a dispute over boundary of the plaintiff and defendants. Resultantly, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 with the help of other defendants threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession from the suit land and they along with other unknown men equiped with deadly weapon on 2-6-2009 at about 10-30 am tried to enter into the suit land. The plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and 5 protested them in presence of local people gathered, then the defendants left the place uttering that they will dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land in future at any time. The defendants have no right, title and possession in the suit property. Because of defendants threat with dispossession the plaintiff has compelled to file the suit for permanent injunction. 

5. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint, contending inter alma that the property covered by SA plot Nos. 384, 385, 386 measuring 2.94 sataks originally belonged to Ahmed Ali and Hatem Ali to the extent of 8 annas (1.47 sataks). Hamed Ali sold 78 sataks of land to Ramjan Ali, Hatem Ali sold 60 sataks of land to Abdul Kuddus by registered deed No. 7319 dated 8-7-1977. Hatem Ali again sold 7½ sataks to Duikkaya Sheikh. Said Abdul Kuddus again sold his purchased land measuring 60 sataks to Ahmed Ali, Hatem Ali and Momtaj Ali, all sons of Ramjan Ali by deed No. 2196 dated 8-2-1984. Said Duikkaya Sheikh sold his purchased land measuring 7½ sataks to Ahmed All and others. In the way aforesaid, Ahmed Ali and his two brothers acquired 1.45½ sataks land by inheritance and by purchase. Each of the brothers equally got 48½ sataks land. Thereafter, Hatem Ali purchased 37½ sataks land from his brother Momtaj Ali by deed No. 12661 dated 28-12-1989 rest 11 sataks of land of Momtaj Ali also got by Hatem by oral exchange. Therefore, Hatem Ali acquired in total 97 sataks of land out of the three SA plots and he was in possession on the northern side. He again sold 32 sataks by a deed No. 7943 dated 18-9-1996 and also transferred 7 sataks of land to Akkas Ali. Thereafter, he sold 26 sataks of land by deed No. 3231 dated 1-4-1997 to one Abdul Razzak. After the transfers aforesaid, only 32 sataks of land remained in the share of Hatem Ali and the said 32 sataks of land was transferred by Hatem Ali to the plaintiffs by registered deed No. 3249 dated 31-4-1997 and deed No. 9623 dated 7-12-1998. The plaintiffs after purchase have been possessing the said 32 sataks of land since 9/10 years. The boundary of the plaintiff by the north Ahmed Ali and south Abdur Razzak. Later on Ahmed Ali from his share by three deed Nos. 6244, 6245, 9025 transferred 40.75 sataks to Shafia Ara, Shahera, Abu Bakkar Siddique, Hafiz and others. Thereafter, Ahmed Ali again acquired 10.75 sataks land by way of Heba-bil-Ewaz and transferred the same to Doctor Ramzan All by a deed No. 5948 dated 21-8-2008 and delivered possession to him. The suit property belong to the defendants, there are no shop house and trees on the suit property belonging to plaintiffs and the houses and the trees are belonging to defendant No. 1. 

6. The defendant No. 1 filed a case against the plaintiffs under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the court of Executive Magistrate, wherein an inquiry was held by Assistant Commissioner (Land) and furnished report finding possession of the defendant No. 1 in the suit property, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

7. The trial court framed three issues for determination of the dispute. In course of hearing the plaintiffs examined five witnesses as PWs and the defendants examined eight witnesses as DWs. Both the parties submitted documents in support of their claim which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon hearing by its judgment and decree dated 28-11-2010 dismissed the suit observing that the plaintiffs failed to prove cause of action for filing the suit. 

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No. 54 of 2011 before the District Judge, Mymensingh. Eventually, the said appeal was transferred to the court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh for disposal who upon hearing by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-1-2014 allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the suit. At this juncture, the defendant-respondents moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

9. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate with Mr Md Ershad Hossain Rashed, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the plaintiffs stated in the plaint, that the defendants tried to enter into the suit land on 2-6-2009 and the cause of action for filing of the suit, but while deposing before the court the plaintiffs witnesses did not say a single word alleging that the plaintiffs were threatened by the defendants on any date in their presence with dispossession. As such, the trial court rightly observed and held that the plaintiffs hopelessly failed to prove cause of action for filing the present suit. He further submits that admittedly, the plaintiffs and the defendants are co-sharers by purchase in the suit plot No. 2565 and there is no legal partition among the parties, as such, the plaintiffs have to file a properly constituted suit for partition but they filed the instant suit for permanent injunction to prevent an admitted co-sharer from enjoying and possessing their purchased land by a decree of permanent injunction. It is also argued that in a suit for permanent injunction, the plaintiffs are to prove the date, time and manner of threat but in the instant case no such allegations have been proved by the witnesses adduced on behalf of the plaintiffs that on which date the defendants threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession. He further submits that in a proceeding under section 144 there was an inquiry report which proves that the defendant No. 1 is in possession of his land and the proceeding was made final by the Magistrate by its order dated 30-8-2009 against the plaintiffs. 

10. He finally submits that for getting a decree of permanent injunction there must be a breach of an obligation existed in favour of the plaintiffs, expressly or by implication and the plaintiffs are to prove that the defendants invades or threatens to invades the plaintiffs right to or an enjoyment of property, but in the present case the plaintiff utterly failed to prove that the defendants threatened the plaintiffs right to or enjoyment of the property by any evidence, therefore, the trial court rightly dismissed the suit, it is also argued that but the appellate court while allowing the appeal failed to appreciate the fact that the plaintiffs utterly failed to prove cause of action for filing of the suit by any evidence as none of the PWs either in the examination-in-chief or in cross examination stated a single word alleging that the defendants threatened the plaintiff with dispossession on any date in their presence and the appellate court also failed to find that the defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit property and he never threatened the plaintiff with dispossession, as such, the judgment of the appellate court is liable to be set-aside. 

11. Mr Abdus Salam Mandol with Mr Khandakar Nazrul Islam, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite parties submit that there is no dispute that the property originally belonged to Hatem Ali and Ahmed Ali and there is no dispute regarding purchase deed of the plaintiffs and admittedly the plaintiffs purchased 32 sataks of land from the suit plot with a specific boundary given in the schedule to the plaint drawing a sketch map showing possession of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and the plaintiffs in the suit plot, therefore, the property is specified with identification. He further submits that the defendants also admitted the purchase of the plaintiffs; the trial court also held that the plaintiffs have title in 32 sataks of land by purchase in the suit plot, but the trial court while dismissing the suit most unfortunately observed that the plaintiff as PW 1 did not say anything about cause of action alleging that they were threatened by the defendants with dispossession. But from record and the evidences led it will be found that the PW 1 in his examination in chief clearly stated that the defendants threatened them with dispossession and in cross examination the defendants did not put any suggestion denying the statement of the plaintiffs, as such, the allegation of dispossession remain unchallenged as no question was put forward to the PW 1 denying such allegation against the defendants. 

12. He further submits that the findings and observations of the trial court are self- contradictory and contrary to the evidences led by the plaintiffs. It is also argued that the appellate court have gone through the plaint and written statement filed by the parties, evidences both oral and documentary and rightly observed that the plaintiff in their plaint at paragraph 5 clearly stated the facts and cause of action for filing the suit. 

13. Moreover, the defendant No. 1 also stated in their written statement that there is a dispute between the par ties regarding boundary and the defendant No. 1 filed a proceeding before the Magistrate Court under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further argued that the appellate court rightly held that the cause of auction is a bundle of fact and to determine cause of action for filing of the suit entire plaint should be considered, accordingly, the appellate court considered the plaint and evidences and found that there is cause of action for filing the suit, as such, the appellate court committed no error in law occasioning any failure of justice, hence, the rule is liable to be discharged. 

14. Heard the learned advocates for the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint, written statement, evidences both oral and documentary and judgment and decree of both the courts below. 

15. From plaint and written statement this Court finds no dispute regarding title of vendors of the plaintiffs and the defendants. SA Khatian No. 119 (Exhibit-Ka) contain plot Nos. 384, 385 and 386 measuring 2.94 acres owned by three groups equally. The defendants claim that their vendors Ahmed Ali and Hatem Ali were owner of 1.45½ sataks land out of three plots. 

16. From perusal of BRS Khatian No. 412 containing only plot No. 2565, this Court finds an area of 1.20 sataks has been recorded in the name of Hatem Ali and Ahmed Ali. Admittedly, Hatem Ali is owner of 2/3rd of the property and Ahmed Ali is owner of 1/3rd of the property. As per BRS khatian Hatem Ali got 80 sataks and Ahmed Ali, the vendor of the defendant No. 1 got 40 sataks only. Both the parties to the proceedings did not raise any question about correctness of BRS khatian finally published in the names of Hatem Ali and Ahmed Ali. In the absence of any objection, considering correctness of the BRS khatian and the sale deeds of the plaintiffs and the defendants it is found that the plaintiffs purchased 32 sataks of land from Hatem Ali by two sale deeds (Exhibits-2Ka and 3) and the rectification deeds (Exhibits-4 and 5). The defendant in their written statement at page 7, paragraph 10(ka) clearly and unequivocally admitted correctness of purchase of the plaintiffs by two sale deeds from Hatem Ali, the relevant portion of which is quoted below: 
“উক্ত ৩২ শতাংশের মধ্যে পশ্চিমাংশের ১০ শতাংশ উক্ত হাতেম আলী বিগত ১-৪-৯৭ইং তারিখে ৩২৪৯ নং সাফ কবলা দলিল মূলে বিক্রয় করিয়া দখল বুঝাইয়া দেয় । বাকী ২২ শতাংশ সম্পত্তি তাহার পূর্বাংশে থাকিয়া যায়। পু��রায় উক্ত ২২ শতাংশ সহ অন্যান্য বেনালিশী দাগের মোট ২৫১/২শতাংশ সম্পত্তি হাতেম আলী বিগত ৭-১২-৯৮ইং তারিখে ৯৬২৩ নং সাফ কবলা দলিল মূলে সুলতান আলী গংদের নিকট বিক্রয় পূর্বক দখল হস্তান্তর করেন। উক্ত সুলতান গং ১০ + ২২= ৩২ শতাংশ সম্পত্তির মালিক দখলকার হিসাবে ৯-১০ বৎসর ভোগ দখল করিয়া আসিতেছে।”

17. From above statement, this Court finds that the plaintiffs are in possession of their purchased land measuring 32 sataks for more than 9/10 years. Purchase deeds of the plaintiffs are earlier than the purchase deed of the defendant No.1. As per BRS khatian, Ahmed Ali owned 40 sataks of land in the suit plot No. 2565 but said Ahmed Ali by a deed No. 9025 dated 18-12-2005 transferred 4 sataks of land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 instead of having title in 3.25 sataks after earlier transfers. 

18. It is in this Court's view that the dispute between the parties arises regarding purchase of 4 sataks instead of 3.25 sataks by defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Para-5 of the plaint shows that there has been a dispute between the parties regarding boundary not regarding their respective possession. The plaintiffs claim that the defendant No. 1 tried to encroach the property of the plaintiffs which has given rise to cause of action for filing of the suit. This Court finds support of such contention from the documents filed by the defendant No. 1 showing that he filed a case against the plaintiffs under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. To appreciate the fact, a relevant portion of the plaint at para-5 are quoted below;

“অতঃপর ১/২ নং বিবাদী নালিশী দাগের উত্তর পূর্বাংশে তাদের খরিদা ০.০৩১/ শতাংশ ভূমি ভোগ দখলে থাকাবস্থায় বাদীগণের স্বত্দখলীয় তপছিল বর্ণিত ভূমি সীমানা অত্যাচার উৎপীড়ন করিতে থাকিলে প্রায়ই ঝগড়া-ফ্যাসাদের সৃষ্টি হয় এবং ১/২ নং বিবাদী অন্যান্য বিবাদীগণের সহযোগীতায় বাদীগণকে নালিশী তপছিল বর্ণিত ভূমি বেদখলের হুমকী দিয়া আসিতে থাকে । অতঃপর সকল বিবাদী পরস্পর যোগ সাজসে পূর্ব পরিকল্পিতভাবে অজ্ঞাতনামা গুন্ডা-পান্ডা লোকজনসহ মারাত্মক অস্ত্রাদিতে সজ্জিতাবস্থায় বিগত ২-৬-০৯ইং তারিখে মোতাবেক বাংলা ১৯শে জৈষ্ঠ্য, ১৮১৬ সাল রোজ মঙ্গলবার, সকাল অনুমান ১০-১০.১/২টার সময় নালিশী তপছিল বর্ণিত ভূমির উত্তর পূর্বাংশে ১/২ নং বাদীর অংশের ০.০৩১/ শতাংশ ভূমির সীমানা অতিক্রম করিয়া বাদীগণের ভূমিতে অনধিকার প্রবেশ করিয়া গাছ বৃক্ষাধি রোপনের উদ্যোগ নিলে ১-৩ নং ও ৫ নং বাদী তাহাদের দোকান প্রতিষ্ঠান হইতে দৌড়াইয়া আসিয়া বাধা প্রদান করিলে বিবাদীগণ মারধোর করার উপক্রম হইলে ৫ লং বাদীর ডাক চিৎকারে জালাল উদ্দিন, পিতা-সৃত আলীম উদ্দিন, আক্তার আলী, পিতা-মৃত ইন্তাজ আলী, শাহাব উদ্দিন, পিতা-হযরত আলী, বাবুল হোসেন পিতা-ইয়াদ আলী, হাতেম আলী, পিতা-মৃত জমির উদ্দিনসহ এলাকার বহু লোকজন জমায়েত হইয়া বিবাদীগণকে প্রতিহত করে। এরপরেও বিবাদীগণ এই মর্মে হুমকী দেয় যে, ভবিষ্যতে সময় সুযোগ মত আর গুন্ডা-পান্ডা লোকজন আমদানী করিয়া জনবলে বলিয়ান হইয়া নালিশী তপছিল বর্ণিত ভূমিতে বিদ্যমান বাদীগণের ও বাদীগণের ভাড়াটিয়াদের দোকান/ব্যবসা প্রতিষ্ঠান ভাংচুর করিয়া বাদীগণকে খুন জখম করিয়া উচ্ছেদ ক্রমে নালিশী সমুদয় ভূমি বেদখল করিবে ।”

19. The above quoted statements made by the plaintiffs in their plaint discloses cause of action for filing of the suit. PW 1 in his examination in chief clearly stated that; 

“আর ও আর রেকডীয় অপর মালিক আহাম্মদ আলী তৎ প্রাপ্ত হিস্যা ০.৪০ শতক জমি হতে ৩টি দলিল মূলে সাফিয়ার নিকট ০.১৩ শতক, ৪নং বিবাদীর নিকট ০.১৬-১/৪ শতক ও সায়েরার নিকট 0.97/53 শতাংশ মোট ০.৩৬৩, শতক ভূমি বিক্রি করেন। অবশিষ্ট ০.০৩-১/৪ শতাংশ থাকলেও আহাম্মদ আলী ০.০৪ শতক ভূমি ১/২ নং বিবাদী বরাবরে কাওলা করে দেয় কিন্তু দখল দেয় ০.০৩-১/৪ শতাংশ ভূমিতে ৷ এমতাবস্থায় কাওলাকৃত বক্রী ভূমি অর্থাৎ আমাদের দখলীয় ভূমির দখল নেয়ার জন্য অবৈধভাবে প্রবেশ করে আমাদের বেদখলের চেষ্টা করে । তখন বাধা প্রদান করি এবং আমার ভাক চিৎকারে জালাল উদ্দিন, আক্তার আলী, আঃ রহমান, শাহাব উদ্দিন সহ বহু লোক উপস্থিত হলে বিবাদপক্ষ ফিরে যায়। কিন্তু ফিরে যাওয়ার সময় বিবাদীগণ ভবিষ্যতে আমাদের বেদখলের হুমকি দেয় । ফলে আমি অত্র মামলা দায়ের করি ।”

20. PW 1 in his cross-examination clearly stated that; 
“বিবাদীরা আমাদের বিরুদ্ধে ফৌজদারী আদালতে মামলা করেছে। এই মামলায় একটি তদন্ত রিপোর্ট দেয়া হয়েছে। এ ব্লিপোর্টে বিবাদীর জমির মধ্যেই তার কলাগাছ, কাঠাল গাছ ও দোকান ঘর আছে মর্মে উল্লেখ করা হয় এবং উক্ত জমি বিবাদীর এবং সেই তা দখল করে। নালিশী জমিতে তার কোন গাছ বা দোকান নেই । নালিশী জমির পূর্ব পাশে বিবাদীর স্বতৃ দখলীয় জমি আছে।”

21. The defendant did not make any cross or put any question suggesting the PW 1 that the defendants did not threaten them with dispossession as alleged by the plaintiffs. Other PWs categorically corroborated each other stating that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit property. In section 144 proceedings the Assistant Commissioner (Land) found possession of the defendant No. 1 in SA plot No. 384 only, but the disputed plot Nos. are 384, 385 and 386 corresponding to BRS plot No. 2565. The defendant No. 1 also in his cross examination as well as in their written statement clearly admitted that the plaintiffs are in possession on the west side of the defendant No. 1. Therefore, there is no dispute that the plaintiffs are in possession. Now the question has come whether the plaintiff could prove cause of action for filing of the suit. 

22. The trial court in deciding issue No. 1 clearly observed as follows: “বাদীপক্ষের দাবী ২-৬-২০০৯ খ্রি. তারিখে নালিশী জমি হতে বিবাদীপক্ষে বাদীপক্ষকে জোরমূলে বেদখলের চেষ্টা করে। বাদীপক্ষের প্রচেষ্টায় ব্যর্থ হয়। কোন ব্যক্তির স্বতু দখলাধীন জমি হতে অপর কোন ব্যাক্তি বেদখলের হুমকি দিলে তাকে আইন অনুযায়ী স্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞার আদেশ দ্বারা বারিত করার সুযোগ রয়েছে। নালিশী জামি হতে বাদীকে উল্লেখিত তারিখে বেদখলের হুমকে প্রদর্শন করায় নালিশের কারন সৃষ্টি হয়েছে এবং উক্ত. বেদখল প্রতিহত করার লক্ষ্যে বাদীপক্ষ অত্র প্রকার মামলা আনয়ন করেছে। এতে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, মামলাটি আনয়নের কারন বিদ্যমান আছে। তাছাড়া নালিশের কারন উদ্ভব ও নালিশী জমির অবস্থান অত্র আদালতের আঞ্চলিক এখতিয়ারের মধ্যে উদ্ভব হওয়ায় এবং মামলার মূল্যমান অত্র আদালতের আর্থিক এখতিয়ারের মধ্যে হওয়ায় এবং আইনের যথাযথ প্রক্রিয়ায় মামলাটি আদালতে দায়ের হওয়ায় অব্র আকারে ও প্রকারে চলতে আইনগত কোন বাধা দেখা যায় না।”

23. The trial court in deciding issue No. 2 clearly observed that:
“প্রদর্শনী ২ক ও ৩ অনুযায়ী বাদীপক্ষের সম্পত্তি ক্রয়ের সত্যতা প্রমাণ মেলে । প্রদর্শনী ১ পর্যালোচনায় নালিশী জমি হস্তান্তরের সময় হস্তান্তর করার অধিকার হাতেম আলীর বিদ্যমান ছিল মর্মে প্রতিয়মান হয় । দালিলিক ভাবে নালিশী জমিতে প্রাথমিক স্বত্ব প্রমাণ হয়। বাদী পক্ষের সকল সাক্ষী নালিশী জমি বাদী পক্ষ দখল করে মর্মে প্রকাশ করে।” But wrongly observed that;

“আরজীতে বিবাদী কর্তৃক বাদী পক্ষকে বেদখলের চেষ্টা করার কথা বলা হলেও এই মামলার মৃথ্য সাক্ষী PW1 জবান বন্দীতে বিবাদী কর্তৃক বেদখল করতে চাওয়ার বিষয়টি উল্লেখ করেন নাই ।”

24. Therefore, the observations and findings of the trial court contradicts each other, in particular, with the observations made in issue No. 1 with issue Nos. 2 and 3. Where the defendants by filing written statement and on oath admitted the title of the plaintiffs and possession in the suit property and admitted that there was a dispute between them and the defendant No. 1 initiated a proceedings under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the appellate court rightly considered all the facts stated in paragraph 5 of the plaint and found cause of action for filing of the suit. 

25. It is true that the plaintiffs and defendant No. 1 are co-sharers in the suit property. The plaintiffs claim that the defendant No. 1 purchased excess property, measuring sataks from Ahmed All for which they tried to encroach the land under possession of the plaintiffs. In this situation, the defendants may institute a suit for partition and until the property is partitioned among the co-sharers by metes and bound, the defendants cannot disturb the admitted possession of the plaintiffs by any means. 

26. In view of the above, this Court finds that though the PWs could not properly state the date of threatening by the defendants with dispossession, but from the evidences, it appears that there is dispute regarding possession and dispossession of the parties which has given rise to a proceedings under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as such, this Court finds that the appellate court in allowing appeal has not committed any error of law occasioning any failure of justice.

27. Taking into consideration the above, this court finds no merit in the Rule. 

28. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs. 

29. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. 

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court records at once. 

End.
